name: Barth across the Sahara and the Sahel
summary: A British-funded mission sets out from Tripoli; its leader James Richardson and its other German member Adolf Overweg die, and Heinrich Barth carries on alone for five years. From his base at Kukawa on Lake Chad he reaches the Benue, Kanem, the Musgu country and Bagirmi; then he crosses the Sokoto caliphate and the Niger to Timbuktu, and comes back down the river past Gao. He learned the languages, copied the chronicles, and wrote the fullest account of the Sahel and its history that Europe would have for a century.

stops.note: The mission of James Richardson, Heinrich Barth and Adolf Overweg sets out with a caravan for Bornu.
Six weeks in the capital of the Fezzan.
Among the Tuareg; on a detour to the haunted Idinen mountain Barth nearly dies of thirst.
The party is held for months in the Aïr mountains by a Tuareg chief.
Barth rides on alone to the city of Aïr and stays for several weeks.
Back to his companions.
The three part, to meet again at Kukawa; Barth goes by Katsina.
The great market city of Hausaland.
The capital of Bornu, by Lake Chad; Richardson has died on the way.
He reaches the great river where the Faro joins it, and guesses it flows to the Niger.
The capital of Adamawa; he is ordered to leave within days.
Back at Bornu.
With Overweg toward Kanem, until Arab raiders turn them back.
Back again.
With the Bornu army on a raid south of the lake, against Mandara and the Musgu.
Home to Bornu with the army's captives and cattle.
The capital of Bagirmi, where no European had been; he is held for months.
Back by 20 August; Overweg dies in September, and Barth goes on alone.
West across Bornu's frontier.
Through Hausaland toward Sokoto.
The caliph Aliyu receives him at his residence near Sokoto.
The seat of the western half of the caliphate.
He crosses the Niger.
Through Liptako.
Seven months in the city under the protection of Sheikh al-Bakkai.
Down the river to the ruins of the Songhay capital.
Back across the Niger.
East again through the caliphate.
Out of money, he borrows at a hundred per cent.
On 1 December he meets Eduard Vogel, sent out because Barth was thought dead.
North with a caravan, by the salt oasis of Kawar.
Back in the Fezzan.
Across the desert to the coast, then by Marseille to London.
